subject: Acme request: RTO/RPO evidence + BCP summary (SIG/CAIQ context)
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BCP/DR evidence request: RTO/RPO details + SIG mapping

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Acme's vendor SIG review we need the following items for Redwood's inference platform:  

- A per-service RTO and RPO matrix (e.g., embeddings, streaming/generation, metadata store, control plane)
- High-level recovery procedures for full-region failure (failover steps, DNS or anycast usage, manual runbooks)
- Most recent DR test results and cadence (last three tests preferred)
- Mapping of the above to SIG/CAIQ questions and any SOC 2 control references you can share (CC7/CC8 or equivalent)

Can you get us an initial bundle by EOD next Tuesday (2026-02-17)? If any items require an NDA or an additional data request, flag them.

Jordan
Security Engineer
Acme Corp

--
Note: we'll likely share this with procurement and InfoSec for final sign-off.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T12:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BCP/DR evidence request: RTO/RPO details + SIG mapping

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short bundle and attached the artifacts below. High level notes up front:  

- We provide service-level RTO/RPO commitments in our SOC 2 scope and in Dedicated contract addenda. For hosted API customers we publish typical RTO/RPO targets (see matrix).
- Recovery approach: primary-region active, multi-region standby with automated failover for control plane; application-level session recovery + KV prefix caching for stateful flows. Failover is DNS with low TTL plus an internal routing plane for faster cutover.
- DR tests: quarterly full failover drills; last full runbook drill completed 2025-11-14 (see DR_Test_Results_2025-Q4.pdf).

Attachments in this thread: Redwood_BCP_Summary_2026.pdf (one-page attestation + control mapping), RTO_RPO_matrix.csv (service rows with RTO/RPO and detection/restore steps), DR_Test_Results_2025-Q4.pdf (post-mortem and lessons learned).

Quick answers to your ask:  
- Per-service RTO/RPO: see RTO_RPO_matrix.csv. Short summary: embeddings: RTO 2 hours / RPO 15 minutes; generation (streaming): RTO 30 mins / RPO 5 mins for stateless requests; control plane: RTO 1 hour / RPO 0 (config backed up across zones).
- Recovery procedures: summarized in Redwood_BCP_Summary_2026.pdf and linked runbook in the Drive folder (shared link below).
- Mapping to controls: the attestation page maps items to CC7/CC8 and to SIG questions; we can provide expanded mapping if you need line-by-line CAIQ entries.

If you'd like, Diego can provide a brief call to walk through the matrix and confirm any region-specific expectations. Also — happy to provide a one-page signed attestation and a DocuSign if procurement wants that.

Next steps: please confirm which artifacts you want redacted (if any) and whether procurement needs a DocuSign attestation.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance (interim)
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_BCP_Summary_2026.pdf (PDF, 1 page); RTO_RPO_matrix.csv (CSV); DR_Test_Results_2025-Q4.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme request: RTO/RPO evidence + BCP summary (SIG/CAIQ context)

Evelyn / Laura — quick internal note before we finalize the deliverable to Acme:  

- Confirming the RTO numbers in the CSV: embeddings service: RTO 2h (we rely on cross-zone warm standby + prefix KV replay). Generation (stateless streaming): 30m. Metadata store (metadata DB): RTO 45m / RPO 1m. Control plane: RTO 1h.
- For RPO we should be explicit about best-effort for queued requests during failover; for Dedicated customers we can provide tighter contractual RPOs.
- Suggest we add a short line in the PDF that clarifies "Failover mechanism: primarily DNS/TLS endpoint swap with internal routing plane; manual escalation checklist included in runbook" — saves back-and-forth with procurement.

I've attached a quick proposed RTO_RPO_table.csv to this internal thread (will include the finalized version in the external bundle). Let me know if you want to tighten any numbers before sending.

—Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BCP/DR evidence request: RTO/RPO details + SIG mapping

Evelyn — got the bundle, thanks. A few clarification items before we hand this to procurement:  

1) Backup retention location: are backups retained cross-region in a separate cloud account or within the same cloud tenant? We need to confirm separation assumptions.
2) Failover orchestration: can you confirm whether the automatic failover path is application-level (session resumption and replay) or largely DNS cutover + manual runbook? The CSV implies both — we need a sentence we can copy into our SIG responses.
3) Can you provide a one-page signed attestation (PDF) confirming the RTO/RPO targets for hosted API and a DocuSign link for procurement?

If you can answer (1) and (2) in-line below and share the attestation, procurement will take it from there. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jordan Lee
Security Engineer
Acme Corp
